items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I did a few things, what free lanced Himber, Bernie Green and radio and television

ctx.x: So then what happened. The war is over. The war ends that year.

I was living in Forestville. I bought a house out here, this place, that was 35 years ago? 1944. Well, then things -- there wasn't too much to be done then. I did a few things, what free lanced Himber, Bernie Green and radio and television and then I'm gradually getting out of the picture.
Still we have the 50's and 60's. What were you doing in the 50's and 60's.

items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Bernie Benny Green gave me a chance to practice some of it

ctx.x: public schools. They didn't even know what the name Schillinger was all about.

So I stuck with it, stuck it out, and then it was a matter of you have to take what you have there and practice it. And Bernie Benny Green gave me a chance to practice some of it, and he, you know, he had that kind of talent that I didn't, and I got very disgusted, discouraged, and I was expecting that this would do the job.

And that why I say I was equipped, and I could understand what the other guys were doing, but you do have to have a certain amount of talent to -- talent in that respect in order to put these things down or to have an idea what to do, and this will just merely give you the technique.
